newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia tax arrears double yr/yr, down in December.
newsitem.headline: Russia tax arrears double yr/yr, down in December.

text.p: Tax arrears in Russia at the start of the year totalled 128.25 trillion roubles, more than twice as much as a year earlier, the State Tax Service said on Thursday.
But tax collection improved in December, cutting the debt by 12 percent, it said in a statement on Thursday.
Arrears included debts to all regional budgets. The tax debt to Russia's federal budget alone totalled 70.5 trillion roubles, the document said.

The failure of Russian companies to pay their taxes was the main cause of the growth in arrears. Mutual non-payments between enterprises and huge debts to the government have choked the Russian economy since the beginning of market reforms in 1991.

As of January 1 a total of 1,665 companies owed more than three billion roubles each to the state budget, making up 62.1 percent of all tax arrears. More than 80 companies owed more than 100 billion roubles each in back taxes and fines.
Tax debt was highest in the energy sector, mainly in Russia's northern regions.

Russia's biggest car company AvtoVAZ was the biggest registered debtor, owing 2.9 trillion roubles, followed by oil companies Noyabrskneftegaz with 1.4 trillion roubles and Nizhnevartovskneftegaz with 1.1 trillion roubles.
The tax service ordered the liquditation of assets of the 31 main debtors worth 43.2 trillion roubles over the past 12 months, but has received only 500 billion roubles.
The statement said a handful of firms had fully paid off their debts. Kavkazstransgas gas pipeline and Irkutskenergo utility have liquidated their tax debts to the budget.
Megionneftegaz oil company and Syzran oil refinery repaid 84 and 66 percent of their arrears respectively.
